intended_object: The summand of the differential that comes from K₃, restricted to the summand G(F₁₂(K₁^{i₁}, K₂^{i₂}), K₃^{i₃}) of the iterated total complex mapBifunctor (mapBifunctor K₁ K₂ F₁₂ c₁₂) K₃ G c₄, i.e. ε₂(i₁₂, i₃) · G(…)(d_{K₃}) followed by the inclusion (or zero). Inferred from the docstring and from how D₃ and the associator construction use it.
explanation:
This is a helper map, not a standard mathematical object. Together with `d₁` and `d₂`, it splits the differential of the iterated total complex into the parts coming from K₁, K₂ and K₃, one summand (i₁, i₂, i₃) at a time. The file then assembles these pieces into `D₁`, `D₂`, `D₃` with `mapBifunctor₁₂Desc`. They exist to compare the two ways of bracketing a triple total complex and so build the associator. The literature has no separate notion called the "third differential on a summand".

The body is still correct. In the iterated total complex, the differential of G(K₁₂, K₃) is ε₁·d_{K₁₂} + ε₂·d_{K₃}. On this summand the K₃ part is therefore ε₂(π(i₁, i₂), i₃) · G(F₁₂(K₁^{i₁}, K₂^{i₂}))(d_{K₃}^{i₃, next i₃}), followed by the inclusion into degree j via `ιOrZero`. That is exactly what the definition writes. Using `c₃.next` is harmless: the lemmas `d₃_eq` and `d₃_eq_zero` show the map is zero when i₃ has no successor and equals the expected formula otherwise.

Because this is an internal piece of the associator construction, the verdict is not_a_mathematical_object.
